**Founding projects:** MCP (Anthropic), Goose (Block), AGENTS.md (OpenAI) [21].

### Governance Principles

- Neutral governance, community-driven development [23]
- Project inclusion based on adoption, quality, community health — not funding [23]
- "Move at the speed of AI" — small, responsive governance [23]
- DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin) required for all commits [24]
- Conventional Commits specification [24]

## Grant Program

Up to $100,000 per grant over 12 months [11]. Focus areas: tool prototyping, MCP integrations, security audits, developer tooling [11]. Milestone-based payments, rolling review, open globally to individuals/small teams not already funded by employer [11].

## Community

- GitHub for code contributions [12]
- Discord for community discussions [7]
- GitHub Discussions active under aaif-goose organization [12]

Block claims 60% of its 12,000 employees use Goose weekly [26]. A separate source claims 50-75% development time savings [28]. Both figures are from secondary sources and were not independently verified.

## Counter-Perspectives

### AAIF Governance Concerns

**Big Tech concentration:** "Heavy involvement of trillion-dollar companies has led some critics to wonder if standards will be steered in ways that favor large corporations" [56]. Platinum memberships confer governance weight [56].

**Transparency uncertainty:** "Transparency in technical steering, contributor agreements and TSC composition will determine whether the foundation truly operates as a neutral steward or merely a vendor consortium" [57].

**Innovation dampening:** "Forming a consortium of competitors could dampen some innovation incentives" [57].

### Agentic AI Category Skepticism

Andrej Karpathy (OpenAI co-founder): AI agents "just don't work" [58]. Gartner: 40% of agentic AI projects expected to be cancelled within two years [58].

### Bus Factor Risk

The general pattern in open source shows projects typically rely on a single developer for ~70% of contributions [56]. While Goose claims 350+ contributors, the distribution of contributions is unknown. Bradley Axen (Block) is identified as the primary creator and maintainer [22].

### Early Stage for Governance Assessment

AAIF was formed December 2025 and Goose was donated April 2026 — governance is less than 6 months old. Too early for meaningful assessment of whether governance promises translate into practice.
